The three-fold purpose of the visit was to commend the Governor and his team for their significant contributions to the stability and growth of the economy, discuss matters of national development, and offer prayers for the Central Bank. Rev. Wengam praised Dr Asiama and his management team for working hard to bring down lending rates, stabilise the cedi, and reduce the rate of inflation. He presented a Holy Bible to the Governor, urging him to be guided by the dictates of the Scriptures in all his endeavours, alongside souvenirs from Assemblies of God, Ghana. Dr Asiama, on his part, called for continuous prayers from the clergy for sustained economic stability. He appealed to religious leaders to use their platforms to educate the citizenry on the critical need to handle and preserve the new currency notes scheduled for release by the Bank of Ghana on December 1, 2026. The Governor also used the occasion to invite Rev. Wengam to serve as the guest speaker for the Bank of Ghana’s 2026 Carols Service. items.title: Atiku’s aide challenges Tinubu over prosperity promise
items.description: A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide evidence of economic improvements under his administration, saying Nigerians need tangible results rather than assurances of future prosperity. Ibe made the remarks in a post on his X handle on Sunday while reacting to Tinubu’s message in Ibadan that Nigeria was on the path to prosperity. He argued that Nigerians needed to see improvements in their living conditions, particularly in the cost of food, transportation, electricity and other essential services. According to him, the President should explain the achievements of his administration and how its policies have translated into better living conditions for citizens, especially as he seeks another term in 2027. Ibe questioned how long households would have to contend with rising living expenses, while workers struggle with increasing costs and businesses face energy-related challenges. He maintained that government claims of economic progress should be assessed against the everyday experiences of Nigerians. On the reported agreement to reopen a vehicle assembly plant, Ibe said productive investment was welcome but argued that its benefits should be measured by the actual resumption of operations, employment opportunities and wider economic impact. He also acknowledged the importance of infrastructure development, while stressing that government should equally account for its impact on the livelihoods of citizens. Ibe further questioned the emphasis on future generations in the President’s appeal for Nigerians to remain committed to the administration’s policies, saying the immediate needs of children and struggling households should also receive attention. He called on the Federal Government to provide Nigerians with a clear account of the outcomes of the sacrifices associated with its policies, including the benefits recorded and when households could expect meaningful relief. Reacting to Tinubu’s remarks about the opposition, Ibe said opposition parties had a legitimate role in scrutinising the administration’s performance, while citizens were entitled to consider alternative political positions. He argued that public confidence in government should be strengthened through responses to citizens’ concerns and demonstrable improvements in their living conditions. Ibe said the benefits of prosperity should be reflected in household purchasing power, workers’ wages, the survival of businesses and the security of communities. He maintained that the administration should provide evidence of its achievements and address the economic and security concerns confronting Nigerians. items.title: Électromobilité : l'ONUDI érige l'automobile marocaine en modèle
items.description: Dans son Rapport sur le développement industriel 2026 dédié à l'Afrique, l'ONUDI s'arrête sur l'écosystème automobile marocain, auquel elle réserve un encadré. Elle y voit la preuve qu'une politique industrielle menée sur la durée peut ouvrir la voie à l'électromobilité. Le document relève toutefois deux fragilités à corriger : la dépendance au marché européen et la faible présence de la filière dans les segments les plus technologiques. En moins de deux décennies, le Royaume a bâti une filière automobile qui lui permet aujourd'hui d'aborder le virage du véhicule électrique. L'ONUDI en décrit un écosystème relativement avancé, qui s'appuie sur les capacités automobiles du pays, ses ressources minérales et ses partenariats avec des constructeurs européens et chinois. Elle le range parmi les expériences africaines de premier plan, aux côtés de celles de l'Afrique du Sud, du Kenya et de l'Éthiopie, où l'assemblage local de véhicules électriques a également démarré. Les chiffres cités par le rapport donnent la mesure de cette dynamique. Les ventes de véhicules ont dépassé le demi-million d'unités en 2024. Celles de véhicules électriques ont progressé de plus de 50 % la même année, pour une capacité de production d'environ 50 000 unités. L'ONUDI les projette à 100 000 unités en 2026. Des groupes mondiaux de premier plan ont, en outre, annoncé des projets à plusieurs milliards de dollars dans les matériaux cathodiques et les batteries, ce qui étend l'ambition de l'assemblage vers la production d'intrants clés. Cette trajectoire remonte, rappelle l'organisation, à la création de la SOMACA en 1959, coentreprise entre l'État marocain et les constructeurs Fiat et Simca. Les partenariats ultérieurs ont attiré les investissements étrangers, d'abord tournés vers le marché intérieur dans les années 1990, puis vers l'export dès le début des années 2000. Les infrastructures ont accompagné le mouvement : routes et voies ferrées relient la Zone franche atlantique de Kénitra au port de Tanger Med, porte d'entrée vers l'Europe et la Méditerranée. L'Accord d'association avec l'Union européenne et la participation à la ZLECAf ont consolidé l'accès aux marchés. Les énergies renouvelables et le recyclage des eaux usées, introduits dans la zone de Kénitra, ont par ailleurs facilité la conformité au mécanisme d'ajustement carbone aux frontières de l'UE, un avantage sur d'autres producteurs en développement. La formation professionnelle, adossée à des partenariats public-privé qui calent les cursus sur les besoins des entreprises, complète le dispositif. Le cas marocain s'inscrit dans un tableau continental contrasté, que le rapport résume sans complaisance. Depuis 2000, la valeur ajoutée manufacturière par habitant n'a progressé que de 0,8 % par an en Afrique, contre 1,9 % pour l'ensemble des pays en développement. Le Maroc est classé dans le groupe des économies à revenu faible et intermédiaire d'Afrique du Nord, avec l'Égypte, le Soudan et la Tunisie, qui pèsent environ un quart de la valeur ajoutée manufacturière du continent. À l'horizon 2050, la poursuite des tendances actuelles triplerait cet indicateur sans combler l'écart avec les régions les plus dynamiques. Un scénario d'industrialisation propre et inclusive le porterait 64 % plus haut, avec quelque 60 millions d’emplois manufacturiers supplémentaires, un PIB par habitant en hausse de 25 % et des émissions de CO₂ inférieures de 9 %. Au-delà de l'automobile, l'ONUDI évoque les capacités nord-africaines dans les engrais et les produits chimiques de spécialité, adossées aux réserves de phosphate. Elle cite le Maroc, avec l'Égypte, parmi les pays qui s'associent à des firmes étrangères pour installer les premières unités photovoltaïques et d'hydrogène renouvelable, en s'appuyant sur le foncier, le climat et les zones économiques spéciales. Elle observe néanmoins que de nombreux projets d'hydrogène vert sur le continent n'ont pas encore atteint la décision finale d'investissement, faute de visibilité sur la demande et les prix. Les points de vigilance restent nets. L'Union européenne a absorbé entre 80 % et 90 % des exportations marocaines de véhicules entre 2004 et 2023, une concentration que l'ONUDI juge risquée dans un contexte d'incertitudes commerciales et de reconfiguration des chaînes de valeur. La montée en gamme passera par les segments à forte intensité de capital et de technologie, notamment les systèmes de batteries et les connecteurs électroniques. Elle suppose aussi que les acteurs de la formation professionnelle actualisent les cursus pour y intégrer des compétences propres au véhicule électrique, comme les systèmes de gestion des batteries et l'ingénierie des logiciels embarqués. The post Électromobilité : l'ONUDI érige l'automobile marocaine en modèle appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Future wars
items.description: THE four-day military confrontation between India and Pakistan last year and the US-Iran war this year have revealed how today’s wars have become far more complex than the conventional conflicts humanity has experienced over millennia. The days of massed soldiery, mechanised armour, and standardised formations are over. Today’s wars are hybrid and employ every instrument of power a state can muster. These wars involve cyberattacks, economic coercion, psychological manipulation through electronic and social media, and cultural invasions. Critically, today’s wars employ lethal technologies, which have left traditional battlefield concepts behind. These autonomous weapons are guided by specialised semiconductors, microchips, and sensors. The changing nature of war has coincided with the sharp descent of the world order into disarray. Wars and armed conflicts between and within states have broken out in various parts of the world. The pledge that all states had made to the UN Charter to respect each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity is no longer being honoured. Two distinguishing features of today’s warfare are advanced missiles and armed drones, which have transformed the nature of war by enabling high-precision, long-range, and rapid response capabilities. In last year’s India-Pakistan war, Pakistan used missiles to down several Indian aircraft flying well beyond visual range. In the US-Iran war this year, both sides relied mostly on missiles guided by infrared sensors and satellite communication rather than conventional confrontation. Autonomous weapons lack the capability to understand the context. Advanced robotic systems are being employed for intelligence, surveillance, and even targeted strikes. Drones and robotic dogs can provide real-time data, improve combat efficiency, and operate for high-risk functions such as clearance of mines or locating captured personnel. Unarmed aerial vehicles provide real-time intelligence, and are equipped with AI-driven capabilities to analyse data. Targets can be independently tracked and even struck by loitering munitions or suicide drones. Transporting supplies and ammunition entails no life losses thanks to unarmed ground vehicles. Drone swarms can now be trained to carry out coordinated attacks. It’s only a matter of time before humanoid robots are deployed for military roles. The spectrum of modern wars employs other technologies as well, such as quantum computing, which solves complex problems faster than classical computers. It ensures unhackable and secure data transmission during conflict situations. Next-generation structural battery composites can store energy for longer periods. Future wars will move further away from face-to-face engagement or human-controlled systems. Intelligent autonomous systems will be central to making decisions, often without human intervention. However, this raises some serious ethical questions. Autonomous weapons lack the capability to understand the context or apply compassion. There is greater likelihood of violating the laws of war and committing war crimes without assigning accountability. Further, the speed and agility of these technologies could cause conflicts to spiral out of control. These technologies will also be used to break an adversary’s morale by targeting its economic assets or supply chains. During the Iran war, for instance, President Trump threatened to destroy Iran’s power grid and bridges, even its civilisation. The kind of technologies a nation possesses will now determine the extent of damage that a future war would impose on an adversary’s policy options. The ability of a nation to acquire and em­­ploy modern technologies is thus critical to both wag­-ing future wars and surviving them. What makes future wars more frequent and unaccountable is the evolving global ecosystem, where use of force has emerged as the primary arbiter of international relations. Major powers have no qualms about using force illegally, unilaterally, and disproportionately to overpower adversaries. In such an uncertain environment, middle and small powers are looking for ways to fend for themselves and make alliances with like-minded countries. This has nudged countries to focus more on R&D for developing not only war-related technologies but also their own digital and satellite-based communication links. That requires a stronger economy, credible information instruments, and creative narrative-building to deter aggression. Diplomatic tools must be geared up to avert such complex multidomain future wars. The world needs a new global compact of indivisible security, akin to the UN Charter, to bind states into mutual respect for each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. This is the only way to avert the devastating wars of the future. The writer is Chairman Sanober Institute and former foreign secretary of Pakistan. Published in Dawn, November 22nd, 2026

items.title: The Relationship That Can Survive Not Talking for Years
items.description: If you don’t speak with a relative for years, you’re probably estranged. If you’re dating someone who’s dropped contact for the past month, you’ve been ghosted. You haven’t heard from your boss in six months? Uh-oh. But one kind of relationship seems to consistently defy the laws of interpersonal physics: friendship. When friends reunite, the fabric of time can pleat seamlessly, allowing them to simply, as the saying goes, pick up where they left off. “Time doesn’t take away from true friendship, nor does separation,” Tennessee Williams wrote in Memoirs . “When we’re together, the years fall away,” Judy Blume once wrote of her best friend, Mary. In the 100 interviews with groups of friends that I conducted for my series The Friendship Files , I often heard similar sentiments. “It was like we’d never been apart,” one person told me of reconnecting with his Army buddies after more than a decade. “It’s as if nothing has changed,” another said of their relationship with friends from kindergarten . If friendship has a superpower, it is the time travel of reconnection. Before these moments, sometimes weeks, months, or years pass with only sporadic communication, if not complete silence. Yet through these fallow periods, friendship can persist without diminishing in strength. I’ve come to think of these empty spaces as friendship’s dark matter. It is the part of friendship we can’t see, directly measure, or definitively prove exists—but we know it’s there, and we feel its effects. In a 1991 paper , Stuart Sigman, a communication researcher, emphasized the importance of the part of relationships that happens in the silence between interactions. “Relationships do not cease after the face-to-face events (conversations) engaged in by co-members are terminated,” he wrote. “In a sense, relationships are ‘larger’ than the physical presence or interactional accessibility of the participants.” Although all relationships have some of this dark matter, friendship is unusual because of how much silence it can survive. Someone doesn’t necessarily lose the title of “friend” just because you haven’t talked to them in a while. With family or romantic partners, a reunion after a long separation could be expected to bring some drama. Yet seeing an old friend is often described as frictionless. [ Read: How friendships change in adulthood ] The nature of friendship allows for this goodwill. “Freedom lives at the heart of friendship,” William Rawlins, an emeritus professor of communication at Ohio University, told me. You can’t choose your parents, but every friendship is created from scratch by the participants themselves. It can take any form they imagine. Cultures have shared expectations for how romantic relationships progress and when families ought to gather. Although couples and families don’t necessarily conform to those scripts, they’re still aware of them. Those cultural guideposts barely exist for friendship. There is no universal prescription for how often friends ought to talk to or see one another. “Our friendship is going to exist as long as we are living up to each other’s expectations of the friendship,” Rawlins said. Friendships can go dormant for a while without dying, he wrote in his 1992 book, Friendship Matters , so long as all parties still think of one another as friends: “The unspoken in friendship, its shared image, may excuse former neglect.” So what is happening when nothing is happening between friends? This is the question Kinneret Lahad, a professor of women’s studies at Tel Aviv University, explored in a paper she published last year. The short answer, as she wrote, is that when nothing happens, “everything happens at the same time.” The full answer is more complicated. “Friendship is imbued with so many sensations, so many intensities that cannot be quantified or qualified or represented in narratives,” Lahad told me. (I’ll try my best to represent some of them in this narrative nevertheless.) Nothing visible or measurable may be happening between two friends; they may be, by all appearances, out of touch. But perhaps they think of each other often. Maybe one helped the other find a job that took them to a new place many years ago; their whole life trajectory remains shaped by that friendship, even though they’re now apart. One friend might see something that makes them think of the other, wonder whether they should reach out, and almost do it, only to hesitate at the last moment. Any or all of that could be happening when a friendship appears dormant. “When nothing is happening in friendship, all of friendship’s ambiguities, possibilities, and constraints are laid bare,” Rawlins said. Lahad’s point is that all of these almosts, maybes, and intangible thoughts still matter. They still affect the friendship and the people within it. This dark matter can, like the universe’s, be the glue that keeps friends together, or it can be the shadows in which misunderstandings and resentments fester. One indirect piece of evidence for the existence of friendship dark matter is that the feeling of closeness between friends is not necessarily linked to how often they are in touch. In a study of long-distance and geographically close friends, Amy Janan Johnson, a professor of communication at the University of Oklahoma, found that although far-flung friends did fewer “maintenance behaviors”—such as calling each other, joking around together, and offering emotional support—that did not mean they felt less connected or invested in the relationship. In fact, she told me, some long-distance friends’ commitment to the relationship was “still increasing.” Johnson suggested that in addition to the active maintenance of talking to and seeing one another, people might also engage in passive maintenance of their friendships by, for instance, looking at old photos and feeling fond feelings, or thinking of someone and wishing them well. These things seem small and ephemeral, but they are ways that friendship can be present even in absence. And they may contribute to the feeling, upon reunion, that the friendship was never interrupted at all. [ Read: Want closer friendships? Move away from your friends. ] Lahad recently published another paper , with her friend and co-author Klara Goedecke, about the feeling of reconnecting after a period of nothingness. And in the most scholarly way possible, they basically said that it’s magic: “Sensed suspension of the sociotemporal order that would otherwise cast time apart as rupture has a ‘mythical’ or ‘extra-temporal’ quality,” they wrote, “which we conceptualize as a sense of wonder.” This wonder is not guaranteed . Let us not over-romanticize the flexibility of friendship; it is completely possible that the dark matter contains not the comforting certainty of continued connection, but confusion and hurt. Friends can drift apart over long separations, and reuniting may be awkward rather than smooth. “Meeting up with an old friend constituted a friendship trial,” Lahad and Goedecke wrote, “a moment where the friendship was put to the test, as it were.” Reconnection comes with risk. Although you may have thought that everything was fine, that it was mutually understood that you still loved each other through the silence, your friend might be upset with you for not reaching out. “Treasured old friendships persist partly as vital (and hopefully mutual) fantasies,” Rawlins wrote. The risk is that the fantasy is not mutual. As technology has made keeping in touch easier and easier, the dark matter of friendship may feel heavier than it did in previous generations. Rawlins and Johnson both pointed out that for those who didn’t grow up with the internet and social media, and had only calls and letters to bridge the distance, long silences between friends may have felt more benign. Friends have so many ways to reach out to one another now that it may feel more fraught when they don’t. This sense that reconnection is risky could be why, as a couple of studies have found , people tend to be reluctant to contact their old friends. Even when they say they’d like to, many hesitate to actually do it. But the risk may not be as high as they think. Another study found that people tend to consistently underestimate how happy those in their social circle are to hear from them. What makes a friendship more or less likely to pick up where it left off? Kristina Castaneto, a psychology Ph.D. student at Simon Fraser University, in Canada, is trying to investigate what makes a person more likely to reconnect with an old friend; her adviser, Lara Aknin, worked on the study about reluctance to reach out. In a recent study , they could not find any personality traits that were linked to someone’s likelihood of getting back in touch. The only thing that seemed to move the needle was a new concept they’ve come up with: friendship resiliency, which they define as “the belief that the friendship will remain despite how much time has passed,” Castaneto told me. That sounds, essentially, like a belief in friendship dark matter. She is still working on developing a way to reliably measure this concept. But it seems possible that the very thing that brings friends back together might be the belief that they’re never truly separated, even when they’re apart. Yet I can’t help but wonder how much this phenomenon is a special property of friendship, and how much it is a survival mechanism in a culture that puts friendship last. Lahad said that she and Goedecke got a similar critique from a colleague regarding their paper on reconnection and wonder. People should be working on their friendships, this person said, not coasting on the assumption that the time apart will collapse when they get back together. The dominant values of American culture—and many other cultures—still say that you should prioritize your work and your family before your friends. When friendship is expected to make way for these other things, people may get used to tolerating lapses in contact, or think that they have no choice but to accept them as part of friendship. The “assumption of benevolence” through a dormant period, as Rawlins put it, can be a beautiful part of friendship. But “at the same time, Julie, at some point, you kind of have to live that with each other,” he told me. You have to prove the benevolent assumption correct. You have to actually pick up where you left off. That’s the thing about friendship dark matter—it can hold the visible matter together … so long as there is some visible matter. Friendship does require taking action, at some point, if you want it to be more than a fond memory. But it is more than the sum of the actions taken. Even if you do make your friends a priority, even if you are regularly in touch, the magic, unmeasurable dark matter remains. Lahad told me about a woman she’d interviewed whose friend had offered her a room to stay in when she was thinking of divorcing her husband. She never took her friend up on it, but just knowing that she had that safety net if she needed it helped give her the confidence to take action and get divorced. Something that wasn’t actually happening was shaping everything. “Friendship also exists in these ways that cannot be boiled down only to how often we meet and how often we talk,” Lahad said. In the dark matter, there is uncertainty, yes. But, as Rawlins said, “the other side of uncertainty is faith.”

items.title: Emir of Daura trends on X after tourist’s ‘inappropriate touching’ allegation
items.description: The Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, has become a subject of controversy on X after a female tourist accused him of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State. The allegation followed the circulation of a video on social media which appears to show the traditional ruler interacting with the tourist during her visit. The woman, who identifies herself online as ‘beduina’, made the allegation in an Instagram post after completing a 30-day trip across different parts of Nigeria. She said the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura. Recounting the encounter, the tourist said she was taken into an elegant room, where she sat with the traditional ruler and engaged in a conversation. She alleged that the Emir held her hand and began playing with it before hugging and kissing her on the cheek. According to her, the encounter took a disturbing turn when the traditional ruler allegedly touched her breasts. “That was a shock for me. I told him ‘emir no, no, no, no’, ‘emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it,” she wrote. The tourist said she was particularly disturbed that the alleged incident happened inside a palace, despite having travelled through different parts of Nigeria without experiencing sexual assault in public spaces. “I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way,” she said. She described the experience as disgusting, adding that she had continued to relive the encounter in her thoughts. The woman said the incident happened a week before she made the allegation public but explained that she waited until she had left Nigeria before speaking about it. She also suggested that other women might have experienced similar treatment from the traditional ruler, although she did not provide evidence of such incidents. “I suspect I wasn’t first woman he assaulted but probably first one with a proof recorded. I have meta glasses and quickly turned them on,” she added. Her allegation has generated reactions on X, with some users expressing concern and demanding accountability. As of the time of filing this report, neither the Daura Emirate Council nor the Katsina State Government had issued an official response to the allegation. The post Emir of Daura trends on X after tourist’s ‘inappropriate touching’ allegation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Guinée : le mérite n’attend plus la mort pour être célébré [Par Aboubacar Sakho]
items.description: Il y a des actions qui méritent d'être soulignées en lettres d'or. Parmi elles figure la reconnaissance du mérite des femmes et des hommes qui consacrent leur énergie, leur compétence et leur dévouement au service de la Nation. J'ai toujours été un partisan des hommages rendus aux personnes de leur vivant, contrairement aux hommages posthumes qui étaient longtemps entrés dans les habitudes en Guinée. Chez nous, il fallait parfois attendre la disparition d'un compatriote pour découvrir ses qualités, reconnaître ses sacrifices et célébrer ses réalisations. Une fois le défunt dans sa tombe, les discours élogieux se multipliaient, les témoignages se succédaient et les grands symposiums s'organisaient. Curieusement, certains de ceux qui avaient été ses adversaires, voire ses pires ennemis de son vivant, devenaient parfois les premiers à chanter ses louanges. C'est dans ce contexte que l'initiative du Président de la République, Son Excellence Mamadi Doumbouya, mérite une attention particulière. Depuis son arrivée aux affaires, le 5 septembre 2021, il a progressivement installé une nouvelle culture de reconnaissance nationale : celle qui consiste à célébrer les mérites des compatriotes pendant qu'ils sont encore en vie et qu'ils peuvent apprécier la considération de leur pays. Cette démarche ne date pas d'hier, elle s'inscrit dans une pratique régulière du Chef de l'État. Au fil des cérémonies, de nombreux Guinéens issus de différents secteurs et de diverses catégories professionnelles ont été distingués pour les services rendus à la Nation. Ce qui retient particulièrement l'attention dans cette démarche, c'est qu'aucun service ne semble être privilégié. Le mérite n'est pas uniquement lié au rang administratif, à la fonction occupée ou au prestige d'un poste. Il concerne aussi bien les hauts cadres que les techniciens, les responsables et les agents qui accomplissent leur travail avec dévouement. La reconnaissance traverse ainsi les différents niveaux de notre administration. Seule la Grande Chancellerie de l'Ordre national du Mérite est véritablement en mesure de donner le nombre exact de Guinéens qui ont été honorés depuis l'arrivée du Général Mamadi Doumbouya aux responsabilités. Mais au-delà des chiffres, c'est surtout cette nouvelle considération accordée au travail et au service rendu qui mérite d'être saluée. Il y a également quelque chose de particulièrement remarquable dans cette démarche : elle permet de sortir de l'ombre des compatriotes dont les parcours professionnels étaient jusque-là peu connus du grand public. C'est notamment le cas d'Elhadj Tounkara, Coordonnateur au Garage du Gouvernement (sur photo). Son nom illustre parfaitement cette volonté de mettre en lumière des hommes qui, loin des projecteurs et des grandes responsabilités officielles, contribuent quotidiennement au fonctionnement de l'État. Voilà toute la portée de cette innovation : donner au mérite une place qui dépasse les titres, les fonctions et les considérations hiérarchiques. Chaque citoyen qui sert dignement son pays peut ainsi voir son engagement reconnu par la Nation. La cérémonie organisée récemment à la Présidence de la République vient une nouvelle fois illustrer cette vision. Plusieurs hauts cadres, responsables et agents de l'administration présidentielle ont été élevés à des distinctions honorifiques au cours d'une cérémonie solennelle coprésidée par le ministre secrétaire général de la Présidence, le Général Amara CAMARA, et le ministre directeur de cabinet de la Présidence, président du Comité stratégique de Simandou, Djiba DIAKITÉ. Le mérite et le dévouement au service de la Nation étaient au cœur de cette rencontre. Plusieurs compatriotes ont reçu les honneurs de la République pour leur contribution professionnelle. La cérémonie a également été marquée par un hommage rendu, à titre posthume, à notre ami feu Fodé Georges SOUMAH, ancien chef de la Division technique et Équipements de la DCI-PRG. Cette distinction rappelle que la reconnaissance nationale concerne aussi ceux qui ont marqué leur passage dans les institutions de la République et dont le souvenir reste attaché au service de l'État. Au fond, cette politique de reconnaissance porte un message fort : le travail bien fait a une valeur, le dévouement mérite considération et le service rendu à la Nation ne doit pas rester sans reconnaissance. Pour ceux qui reçoivent ces distinctions, c'est une fierté personnelle et familiale. Pour les autres travailleurs, c'est une source d'encouragement et une motivation supplémentaire. Il faut reconnaître au Général Mamadi Doumbouya cette innovation dans la manière de célébrer les serviteurs de la République. En donnant aux hommages une dimension plus vivante, il contribue à faire évoluer une tradition longtemps marquée par les célébrations posthumes. Car, finalement, quel bonheur pour un homme ou une femme de pouvoir entendre, de son vivant, les témoignages de reconnaissance de son pays, de recevoir une distinction nationale et de partager cette fierté avec sa famille et ses proches ! Honorer les mérites de son vivant, c'est donner à la reconnaissance toute sa véritable signification. C'est aussi une belle manière de dire à ceux qui servent la Guinée que leur travail compte et que la Nation ne les oublie pas. Aboubacar SAKHO Expert en Communication L’article Guinée : le mérite n'attend plus la mort pour être célébré [Par Aboubacar Sakho] est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Faso Talent d’or 2026 : Chérifa Sanon décroche le grand prix d’une valeur de 2 millions de FCFA
items.description: La 4e édition de la compétition Faso Talent d'or 2026 a refermé ses portes avec la cérémonie de remise de prix aux lauréats, le samedi 21 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Au terme de cette cérémonie, la créatrice de contenu Chérifa Sanon a été sacrée Faso Talent d'or 2026. Elle repart avec une récompense de 2 millions de FCFA. Après une première phase de sélection marquée par les votes du public, le suspense a pris fin avec la proclamation des résultats. Parmi les candidats en lice, Chérifa Sanon s'est particulièrement illustrée en remportant le grand prix de cette quatrième édition. Ahmed Yessoufou, le promoteur du Faso Talent d’or s’est exprimé satisfait Pour le promoteur du Faso Talent d'or, Ahmed Yessoufou, cette édition est une source de satisfaction au regard du déroulement de la cérémonie. « C'est un sentiment de satisfaction pour tout ce qui s'est passé. Ce fut une belle soirée. Tout le monde est reparti avec son trophée et son enveloppe », a-t-il confié. Selon le promoteur, le Faso Talent d'or entend mettre en lumière des talents qui peinent parfois à bénéficier de la visibilité qu'ils méritent. S'adressant aux candidats, Ahmed Yessoufou a salué leur engagement et les a encouragés à poursuivre leurs efforts. « Être nominé, c'est déjà une victoire. Repartir finaliste, c'est une deuxième victoire, et repartir lauréat, c'est une consécration », a-t-il déclaré. Sacrée Faso Talent d'or 2026, Chérifa Sanon n'a pas caché sa joie. Créatrice de contenu et promotrice d'une marque de vêtements, elle considère cette distinction comme une reconnaissance de son travail et de sa passion. « Je remercie le comité d'organisation parce que j'ai été nominée dans la catégorie créatrice de contenu. C'est quelque chose que je faisais par passion. Voir qu'aujourd'hui je suis finaliste et que je remporte le prix de Talent d'or de l'année, je suis vraiment honorée », a-t-elle exprimé. Chérifa Sanon, sacré Faso talent d’or décide de consacrer la moitié du montant reçu pour des œuvres caritatives La lauréate consacre ses contenus à la valorisation de la culture et du patrimoine. Ses publications mettent notamment en avant les activités culturelles, les sites touristiques et les richesses du Burkina Faso. Chérifa Sanon a confié qu'une partie du montant remporté sera consacrée à une activité communautaire en faveur des personnes dans le besoin, tandis que l'autre partie servira à acquérir du matériel de meilleure qualité afin d'améliorer ses productions audiovisuelles. Outre le grand prix, plusieurs autres distinctions ont été décernées au cours de la soirée. Il s'agit notamment des prix du meilleur jeune artisan, du meilleur jeune entrepreneur innovant, du meilleur artiste de l'année, du meilleur acteur de l'industrie culturelle et créative, de la femme d'impact, du meilleur créateur de contenu, du meilleur créateur de mode (catégories designer et crochet), du meilleur jeune photographe, du meilleur jeune talent du micro et du meilleur acteur du 7e art. Dans chacune de ces catégories, les lauréats ont reçu un trophée, une attestation et une enveloppe de 200 000 FCFA. Remise d’attestation au meilleur photographe de l’année Notons que le Faso Talent d'or est une initiative déployée dans quatre pays, à savoir le Gabon, le Togo, la Côte d'Ivoire et le Burkina Faso. items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni A 70-year-old woman has survived after accidentally falling into a 60-foot-deep well at Oworonshoki, Kosofe Local Government Area of Lagos State. items.title: PTI MNAs demand to know whereabouts of party leaders detained in KP, seek their court production
items.description: ISLAMABAD: PTI lawmakers from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday reiterated their demand for the immediate disclosure of the whereabouts of all detained PTI leaders and workers, their production before the courts and the provision of their legal right to defence. The demand was made during a meeting of PTI’s elected members of the National Assembly (NA) from KP, held in Islamabad under the prevailing political and constitutional situation, according to a statement by the party. At the meeting, the lawmakers called for the immediate disclosure of the whereabouts of now non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, provincial president Junaid Akbar Khan and other detained party leaders and workers. Afridi — whose role as the chief minister was rendered non-functional due to governor’s rule — Swati and some other lawmakers have been in “ preventive detention ” since emergency was imposed, according to police. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also said last month that Afridi and Swati had been placed under house arrest . The lawmakers expressed serious concern over the alleged arrests and undisclosed whereabouts of Afridi, Swati, Junaid Akbar Khan, MNAs Dr Amjad, Fazal Muhammad Khan, Naseem Shah, Iqbal Afridi and Zubair Wazir, along with provincial ministers and MPAs. They demanded that all detained elected representatives be immediately brought before the public and produced before the relevant courts. “Their families should be informed about the reasons for their arrests and places of detention, while they must be granted the full legal right to defend themselves,” the statement said. The PTI members stressed that depriving elected representatives of their political activities and keeping them in undisclosed detention amounted to an assault on democratic values and the public mandate. In last month’s comments on detentions after governor’s rule, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry had said those with cases against them will be tried, while others would be released. The participants also condemned the recent detentions of former provincial minister Taimur Saleem Jhagra, Kamran Bangash and Irfan Saleem under the MPO, asserting that their arrests despite protective bail granted by the Peshawar High Court raised serious questions about respect for judicial orders and the rule of law. The PTI lawmakers demanded that the three leaders be immediately produced before the court, released and provided with all legal facilities, the statement said. Former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, along with MNAs Atif Khan, Saleem Rehman, Sahibzada Sibghatullah, Mehboob Shah, Shahram Khan Tarakai, Shahzada Gastasap, Muhammad Nawaz Khan, Asif Khan, Ali Asghar Khan, Arbab Sher Ali, Sohail Sultan, Ali Khan Jadoon, Sajid Momand, Shah Ahad and Bashir Khan, attended the meeting. The PTI statement comes a day after it emerged that President Asif Ali Zardari promulgated an ordinance, doing away with most of the “privileges” of KP lawmakers, including protection against “preventive detention”. Through an amendment ordinance related to the privileges of MPAs, drastic changes have been made in the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act 2026, as 21 of its 40 sections have been omitted, including those providing protection to the MPAs against “preventive detentions” and offences related to “breach” of privileges. Four other ordinances promulgated provided a legal framework for special initiatives in the designated 12 districts and other districts in the province. With the imposition of emergency in KP on Oct 11, an Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) was formed to oversee 12 districts that were deemed to face intense security challenges, including the merged districts. On governor’s rule and ongoing political situation The meeting also condemned reported raids on the homes of PTI workers and detentions under MPO following the imposition of governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11. The participants alleged harassment of political workers, violation of the sanctity of homes and restrictions on political activities, condemning them as “blatant violations of the Constitution and fundamental human rights”. They demanded the immediate release of all detained party workers. Rejecting the imposition of governor’s rule in KP on the pretext of terrorism, the meeting asserted that the PTI provincial government had consistently adopted a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism. The participants said terrorism could not be “used as a political tool to undermine the democratic mandate” of the province. They called for the immediate and effective implementation of the National Action Plan and strict adherence to a resolution adopted by all political parties in KP. During the meeting, PTI leaders claimed that governor’s rule had further aggravated the province’s political, economic and administrative challenges. It also criticised KP Governor Kundi, saying that instead of representing the federation and playing a constructive role in resolving provincial issues, his actions were further complicating the situation. The participants expressed “serious concern” over delays by the federal government in releasing KP’s financial entitlements and deductions from its resources. They said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had promised Rs160 billion to the province, but under a new agreement, the federal government had made deductions of approximately Rs157bn, which they termed an injustice to the people of the province. According to the statement, they contended that the federal government was “treating the province like a stepchild” under the pretext of governor’s rule and stressed that the people of the province could not be deprived of their constitutional and financial rights. The meeting also expressed concern over the withdrawal of security provided to JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman. The participants maintained that ensuring the security of all political leaders, irrespective of political differences, was the responsibility of the state. They demanded that Fazl and other leaders of his party be immediately provided with the required security. The participants welcomed PPP scion Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s statement describing Imran as a political prisoner and his support for PTI’s position on the reserved seats issue. They termed Imran a major political stakeholder and said that attempts to exclude him from the political process were detrimental to democracy. They stressed that the PPP should go beyond statements and take practical steps, calling for Bilawal to dissociate himself from the imposition of governor’s rule and not vote for its extension in the NA. The meeting concluded with a “reaffirmation of the participants’ commitment to the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law, the protection of political freedoms, safeguarding the province’s constitutional and financial rights, respect for the public mandate and ensuring the security of all political leaders”, the statement added. PTI seeks Imran’s access to personal physician According to the statement, the meeting also discussed in detail the health and treatment of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, the law and order situation in KP, concerns over the imposition of governor’s rule, the province’s constitutional and financial rights, and the overall political situation in the country. Imran has been in prison since Aug 5, 2023 , while his wife was arrested on Jan 17, 2025 in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced. The IHC has allowed him twice-a-week meetings with his family, lawyers and other associates, but despite multiple court directives , the meetings have been largely restricted . Imran and Bushra’s lawyers were able to meet the couple earlier this month after a gap of several months , after the Islamabad High Court issued directives for the meeting to aid legal consultation. In the meeting, PTI lawmakers demanded that all facilities be provided to Imran in accordance with the jail manual and Supreme Court (SC) judgments. They called for him to have immediate access to his personal physician and for the restrictions on meetings with his family, lawyers and political leaders to be removed, maintaining that any negligence or unnecessary restrictions concerning his health and safety would be unacceptable. The meeting also strongly condemned the detention of Imran’s sister Aleema Khan , held since late September under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance (MPO), and demanded her immediate release. It called for Bushra Bibi’s release as well and demanded that she be provided justice in accordance with the law. According to the statement, the participants further demanded that cases against Dr Yasmin Rashid, Shah Mahmood Qureshi, Mahmoodur Rashid, Ejaz Chaudhry and other detained PTI leaders and workers be decided on merit, without political victimisation.

items.title: Atiku’s aide faults Defence Ministry over Tinubu rally publicity
items.description: A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has questioned the use of the Ministry of Defence’s official social media platforms to publicise a campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid. Ibe, in a post on his X handle on Sunday, faulted the ministry for allegedly using its official Facebook page and X account to announce the rally and publicise Defence Minister, General Christopher Musa’s inspection of the venue ahead of the event. He argued that the development raised concerns about the use of government communication platforms for partisan political activities. According to him, while providing security for a presidential visit falls within the legitimate responsibilities of the ministry, using its official platforms to promote a re-election campaign compromises the institutional neutrality expected of public institutions. Ibe noted that the Ministry of Defence was funded by taxpayers across different political affiliations and should, therefore, serve the interests of all Nigerians rather than those of a particular political party. He said Nigerians facing insecurity deserved information about government efforts to protect their communities and support military personnel, rather than publicity for political campaigns. He also questioned the confidence opposition parties and voters could have in the impartiality of state institutions if official government communication platforms were used to promote activities associated with the ruling party. Ibe called on the Defence Minister to explain the publication, ensure the removal of what he described as partisan campaign publicity and maintain a clear distinction between official government responsibilities and party activities. items.title: NAFDAC destroys N22.73bn fake, unsafe products, records 52 arrests
items.description: … 821 seizures, 179 premises shut in eight months By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed unwholesome products valued at approximately N22.73 billion, seized 821 products and secured 52 arrests in eight months as it intensified enforcement against unsafe and substandard regulated products. The agency disclosed that it carried out 5,542 enforcement activities, including 213 raids, between January and August 2026, while 179 premises were shut and 221 sanctions imposed. The figures formed part of major regulatory milestones presented by NAFDAC at the International Pharmaceutical Regulators Programme (IPRP) Management Committee Meeting in Prague, Czech Republic, held from November 18 to 19, 2026. The agency also reported progress in local pharmaceutical manufacturing, disclosing that more than 70 per cent of finished pharmaceutical products covered by its 5+5 policy and Ceiling 36 are now being manufactured in Nigeria. The development is expected to reduce dependence on imported medicines and strengthen the country’s medicine security. In its regulatory update, NAFDAC said it had sustained its World Health Organisation (WHO) Maturity Level 3 status and was working towards attaining Maturity Level 4, the highest level of the WHO Global Benchmarking Tool. It identified digital innovation as a critical component of the transition, citing the Integrated Regulatory Information Management System (IRIMS), Performance Management System (i-PMS), GMP Inspection (GMPi), Application and AI-assisted Technical Screening Tools (TST), and the revised Med Safety App. The revised application is designed to strengthen the reporting of adverse drug reactions and substandard and falsified medical products. NAFDAC also highlighted Nigeria’s growing influence in African pharmaceutical regulation, noting that it had emerged as a reference National Regulatory Authority, hosting regulatory authorities from Uganda, The Gambia, Mozambique and Côte d’Ivoire for technical capacity building and institutional benchmarking. Another milestone was Nigeria’s ratification of the African Medicines Agency (AMA) Treaty, with the instruments of ratification deposited on October 25, 2026. The agency said the achievements reflected the strategic leadership of its Director-General, Prof. Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye, and ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional capacity, promote science-based regulation and deepen international regulatory cooperation. NAFDAC reaffirmed its commitment to protecting public health, strengthening Nigeria’s pharmaceutical industry and positioning the country as a leading regulatory authority in Africa. items.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Atiku demands probe, overhaul of water transport safety
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has called for an investigation into Friday’s fatal boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, urging the Federal and State Governments to strengthen safety measures on the nation’s waterways to prevent further loss of lives. Atiku said the tragedy, which claimed several lives, highlighted the risks faced by millions of Nigerians who rely on boats for daily transportation, particularly in riverine communities, and called for urgent government action to protect them. In a statement on Sunday, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan, described the incident as a heartbreaking tragedy that had plunged the affected communities into mourning. He said the victims were travelling to honour a departed loved one when the accident occurred. “What makes this tragedy even more painful is that these were ordinary Nigerians who set out in love and solidarity to honour a departed loved one, only to meet their own untimely deaths on the waters,” Ologbondiyan said. “Bayelsa has lost fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners. No words can adequately capture the depth of grief now hanging over the affected communities.” Ologbondiyan commended local divers, the Marine Police, the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other emergency responders for their efforts in the search and rescue operations. He, however, called for a thorough investigation into the cause of the mishap and stricter enforcement of regulations against boat overloading, the use of unseaworthy vessels and other unsafe practices. He said preventing similar accidents would require sustained government investment in safer water transportation. “The Federal and State Governments must prioritise the provision of standard and well-maintained boats, adequate life jackets, functional jetties and properly trained boat operators across riverine communities,” he stressed. “For millions of Nigerians in the Niger Delta and other riverine areas, water transportation is not a luxury; it is a daily necessity. Their safety must never be treated as an afterthought.” He also urged the Federal Government, Bayelsa State Government and relevant humanitarian agencies to provide immediate assistance to survivors and bereaved families. Such assistance, he said, should include medical care, psychosocial support and financial help with the burial of victims. Atiku commiserated with the bereaved families, the people of Ayama and Ukubie communities and the Bayelsa State Government, while praying for the repose of the deceased and the speedy recovery of those injured. The post Bayelsa boat tragedy: Atiku demands probe, overhaul of water transport safety appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: «Kill list» ukrainienne Myrotvorets : Meloni interpelle Zelensky, Salvini menace l’aide militaire à Kiev
items.description: Matteo Salvini ne compte pas laisser passer son inscription sur la liste ukrainienne des cibles a eliminer, Myrotvorets. Le differend a gagne Berlin, ou Giorgia Meloni aurait demande personnellement a Volodymyr Zelensky le retrait des noms de plusieurs responsables politiques italiens, rapporte Il Fatto Quotidiano . Elle lui aurait lance : « Volodymyr, c'est inacceptable tant pour Salvini que pour tous les Italiens ». L'affaire a eclate le 19 novembre, quand l'inscription de Salvini a refait surface. Elle remonte pourtant au 27 avril 2017, selon La Stampa . Le dirigeant de la Ligue est notamment vise pour son voyage en Crimee en 2014 et ses positions concernant la Russie. Salvini met en cause l'aide a Kiev Invite de Tg2 Post le 19 novembre, Salvini a lie le vote sur les livraisons d'armes a des excuses de Zelensky et a une condamnation du site. Il a declare : « S'il n'y a pas de dementi, de condamnation ou de prise de distance, nous en tirerons les conclusions. » Ajoutant enfin : « J'attends des excuses de la part de Zelensky. » Salvini n'a pas annonce de veto. Il attend de connaître la proposition qui sera soumise au vote. Le dispositif autorisant les livraisons militaires a Kiev prend fin le 31 decembre. La querelle porte donc aussi sur les decisions que Rome devra prendre pour 2027. Le lendemain, Salvini a demande la fermeture de Myrotvorets, denoncant des methodes de fichage qu'il qualifie de nazies. Il a affirme : « J'espere que les autorites ukrainiennes fermeront ce site qui diffuse notamment des messages de haine et de mort ». Un site deja denonce a Bruxelles Myrotvorets publie des fiches sur des personnes presentees comme hostiles a l'Ukraine, avec parfois leurs donnees personnelles. Des eurodeputes italiens du Mouvement 5 etoiles ont eux aussi recemment ete ajoutes a la liste. a Bruxelles, Roberta Metsola, presidente du Parlement europeen, veut demander des explications a Kiev. Le ministre italien des Affaires etrangeres, Antonio Tajani, a fait de meme. La controverse ne date pas d'hier. Des fevrier 2021, le Parlement europeen reclamait l'interdiction des activites de Myrotvorets et de sites similaires, pointant les risques d'incitation a la haine et la divulgation de donnees personnelles. Le site est pourtant toujours actif, cinq ans plus tard. Fatto Quotidiano precise que Salvini n'avait toujours recu aucune excuse officielle lors de la parution de son article. Le vice-Premier ministre attend toujours une reaction de Zelensky, a quelques semaines du vote sur l'aide militaire.

items.title: PSG confirm Desire Doue ruled out for months with torn ACL
items.description: Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue has suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee, the reigning French and European champions confirmed on Sunday. Doue, 21, went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half of Saturday’s 3-2 Ligue 1 win at Nice and was stretchered off in tears. The French international will undergo surgery before the end of the month, PSG added in a brief statement, without specifying the expected length of his absence, which is likely to be a matter of months. Doue looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow him to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. PSG have also lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too. “It is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique said on Saturday night. The French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in their Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns. He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently.
